attacks.claim: The cost model mixes time bases. 38M lines/day x 60 tokens is 2.28B tokens per day, so ~$1,140 is the daily input cost. The output figure (8,640 summaries/day x 400 tokens, ~$7) is also daily. Monthly cost is therefore ~$34,000, about 23x the $1,500 budget, and the design as specified is unaffordable. Peak days (61M lines) and per-call prompt overhead are not costed either.
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140" ... "Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget."

attacks.claim: Staffing ignores the stated on-call load. Both engineers are in the rotation with ~50% interrupt work, so two engineers for 6 weeks give about 6 effective eng-weeks, not 12. The estimate has no buffer, and the schedule is unsound.
attacks.evidence: "Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)."

attacks.claim: Redaction is only stated to cover emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs, and was audited for the retention policy, not for third-party LLM egress. Names, customer IDs and free-text payloads may pass through. Every application log line is sent to an external provider. The DPA/zero-retention claim does not say whether it covers this endpoint, training use, region or subprocessors.
attacks.evidence: "which already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)." / "zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417)"

attacks.claim: No failure handling is defined for the LLM dependency (timeouts, retries, 429s, outage) or for stale or misleading summaries attached to pages. Summaries can be up to 5 minutes old, with no staleness labelling, kill switch or rollback for the PagerDuty auto-comment.
attacks.evidence: "Summaries are advisory only." ABSENT: staleness timestamps, degradation behavior, kill switch for the auto-comment

attacks.claim: log-tap sits on the live Vector production log pipeline with no backpressure, isolation or bounded queue. A slow summarizer, Redis or a log storm could stall or drop logs that on-call also depends on. There is no per-window token cap or spend circuit breaker.
attacks.evidence: "subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline after the redaction stage and forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue."

attacks.claim: The launch gate rests on 40 incidents graded by a single incident commander who already knows the outcomes. That sample cannot bound a 5% misleading rate. The MTTR target is also not backed by a breakdown showing that grep time dominates MTTR.
attacks.evidence: "Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading." / "Target: median MTTR 47 min -> 30 min"

attacks.claim: Untrusted log content goes straight into the prompt and the output is posted into incident comments, with no sanitization or output validation (prompt injection). Access controls for log-tap, the queue and the stored summaries are not described.
attacks.evidence: "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt"

attacks.claim: The design is bound to a single proprietary model with no fallback or provider abstraction, and no data residency is stated.
